name: Superman
summary: Face down, lift the arms and legs a centimetre or two off the floor, hold, lower.
setup: Lie on your front, side-on to the phone at floor level, arms overhead. Lift arms, chest and legs off the floor together, hold two seconds, lower slowly.
brief: Lie on your front, arms overhead. Lift arms, chest and legs off the floor together, hold two seconds, lower slowly.
why: From the side the shoulder line rises against the hip each rep, so reps are counted. Lifting too high is not judged.
tempo: Lift 2 s, hold 2 s, lower 2 s.
progression: Longer holds; add a light hand weight.
regression: Arms only, then legs only — or swap to the bird dog.
contraindications: Any lower-back pain. A full superman puts a lot of compression through the lower back — if your back is irritable, do the bird dog instead, which trains the same muscles for far less load.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Lifting arms and legs high
faults.tip: A big arch loads the lower joints of the spine hard. A centimetre with a long reach is the aim — if your back is irritable, use the bird dog instead.

faults.label: Lifting too high
faults.tip: Higher pinches the lower back; a small lift with a long reach is the aim.

faults.label: Looking up
faults.tip: Lifting the head extends the neck along with the back and adds nothing.

faults.label: Looking up
faults.tip: The head stays in line with the spine.

guide.cannotSee: How high the legs are — the arms hide them.

points.t: Chest and arms lift a little; long reach.
